howto.goal: Get four of your pieces in a row — across, down, or diagonally — before the other side does.
howto.setup: A seven-column, six-row grid. Pieces fall to the lowest empty slot. White moves first.

sections.title: Dropping
sections.text: Click a column and your piece lands at the bottom of that column. You cannot drop into a full column.

sections.title: Four in a row
sections.text: Four touching pieces in any straight line wins: across, down, or diagonally.

sections.title: Blocking
sections.text: If the other side has three in a row with an open end, take that square first.

controls: Click a column to drop your piece.
Hover a column to see where the piece would land.
Undo in a learning game takes back your last move and the computer's reply.

frames.say: A piece lands at the bottom.

demo.intro: Watch a short computer game: both sides drop pieces, and black has to answer white's threat.

lines.say: Empty grid. The middle columns are strongest because they reach the most lines.
White drops in the middle column.
Black answers in the same column, stacking underneath.
White starts a second line beside it.
White spreads wider, building two threats at once.
Black takes the open side. Two threats is how this game is won.

demo.outro: Look for a move that creates two threats at once. Your opponent can only block one.

steps.say: Click the middle column to drop your first piece.
Now build a line of three pieces in one direction.
Watch for the computer's three in a row and block the open end.
Aim for a move that makes two threats at once — it cannot block both.
